Every telescope gets a first light — the first night you actually point the thing at the sky after however many months of building it. It is traditionally underwhelming. Something is out of collimation, the finder is off, and you spend the evening fixing rather than looking.

This is that. The site exists, the sections are laid out, and nothing is in them yet.

What goes here

Six sections, arranged along a scale bar from the atomic lattice out to the observable edge. Optics at the small end, telescopes at the large end, and everything in between placed roughly where its subject actually lives. The gap in the middle is real: there is not much between a workbench and a galaxy that I have opinions about.

More soon.
